content.title: Karol G Makes History as First-Ever Latina to Headline Coachella: 'We Want Everyone to Feel Welcome'
content.text: NEED TO KNOW Karol G became the first-ever Latina to headline Coachella on Sunday, April 12The Colombian star performed a roughly 90-minute set and brought out Becky G, Cigarettes After Sex's Greg Gonzalez and moreKarol made her festival debut in 2022 Karol G has made history as the first Latina to ever headline Coachella. On Sunday, April 12, the Colombian singer took the stage for her headlining performance at the music festival in Indio, Calif. During her set, filled with technicolor light displays, fireworks, waterworks and palpable energy from the crowd, Karol spoke about becoming the first Latina headliner at Coachella and gave a shoutout to her Latino compatriots. "I want to present myself. I am Carolina from Medellín, Colombia and today I am the first Latina woman to headline Coachella. And I’m very happy and very proud about this but at the same time it feels late. There has been 27 years of this festival going on and it’s the first time a Latina girl is headlining Coachella," Karol told the crowd. "I just want to say that before me there were so many great Latino artists, legendary Latino artists, that gave me the opportunity to be here tonight. So this is not just about me, this is about my Latino community, this is about my people. And at the same time, this is for my Latinos that have been struggling in this country lately. We stand for them, I stand for my Latino community and at the same time I’m very proud because this brings out the best of us: unity, resilience, and a strong spirit." Karol also acknowledged the strife that many in the Latino community in the United States are experiencing now. The community's hardship, Karol said, was all the more reason to give her Coachella performance her all: her historic set is a huge way to celebrate music's role in Latino culture, and to invite others to celebrate, too. "We do this because we want everyone to feel welcome to our culture, to our roots, to our music, so I just want everyone to feel proud of where you come from, please," she said. "Don't feel fear. Feel proud. Raise your flag." Karol G performs at Coachella in Indio, Calif. on April 12, 2026. Katie Flores/Billboard via Getty During her roughly 90-minute set, Karol brought out a number of additional artists. Per Rolling Stone, she ushered in Mexican-American pop singer Becky G for a mariachi rendition of "Mamii"; reggaetón artist Wisin for a four-song stretch; Cigarettes After Sex singer-guitarist Greg Gonzalez, who joined her to debut their song "Después de Ti"; and Arturo Sandoval, a Cuban-American jazz trumpet player who featured in "Ivonny Bonita." In addition to Karol, Justin Bieber, Sabrina Carpenter and Anyma were also headliners at the festival. Days before the festival, the "Provenza" singer appeared on the cover of Playboy magazine and opened up about her headlining performance. Related Stories “When I received the call, I felt like a huge weight fell on me. They called me and told me — in Spanish — that I was going to be the first Latina to close the festival," the "Tusa" singer said. "I feel like it's a show for my community, for the world, but it's a show that's very much for me," she continued. Karol made her festival debut in 2022 and paid tribute to her Colombian roots with a special medley. She also brought out longtime friend J Balvin for a performance of his smash hit "Mi Gente." Karol G performs at Coachella in Indio, Calif. on April 12, 2026. Her headlining performance at Coachella also follows the release of her fifth studio album Tropicoqueta, which came out in June 2025 and symbolized a reclaiming of herself. In 2024, Karol opened up to PEOPLE about the ending of her Mañana Será Bonito era, which earned her a Grammy for Best Música Urbana Album. "I'm full of emotions. I can't believe that something this big came off one of the hardest moments of my life," she said.
